# How to Ask Alexa+ for Weather-Based Outfit Suggestions

> **In short:** Alexa+ can answer a single question that covers both today's forecast and what to wear, and may remember your preferences for next time. The trick is asking for weather *and* clothing in one sentence, and saving your preferences so you don't have to repeat them every morning.

You already know how to talk to Alexa+. This guide adds one morning routine that pays back every day: asking for clothing ideas that actually match the weather, your schedule, and your style — without opening a forecast app, a calendar, or your closet, all at the same time.

## Before you start
- An **Alexa+ enabled** Echo device, or the Alexa+ app on your phone. Alexa+ is Amazon's newer assistant experience; confirm your device or app shows the Alexa+ branding before you begin.
- A working Amazon account linked to that device or app. Whether Alexa+ requires an extra paid plan, or comes bundled with another Amazon membership, varies by region and over time — check Amazon's official Alexa+ page for the most current details.
- About **3 minutes** the first time, under a minute on regular mornings once your preferences are saved.

## Step 1 — Ask for weather and outfit in one sentence
Wake Alexa+ with your usual wake word, then ask **one question that covers both the data and the intent**. A simple "Alexa, what's the weather?" gets you a forecast — but if you also ask what to wear, the assistant has a clearer picture of what you actually want. Speak the way you would to a friend, then pause for the response. On an Echo with a screen, you may see a forecast card appear while Alexa+ speaks; on a speaker-only Echo, you'll just hear the answer. If your device uses a custom wake word, say that instead. Honest limit: Alexa+ can suggest clothing, but it can't see your closet — it works from the weather and whatever you tell it about your style.
💬 Example: "Alexa, what's the forecast for today, and what should I wear?"
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ answers with both the day's weather **and** at least one concrete clothing suggestion — not just a temperature reading.

## Step 2 — Add context about your day and your style
The first answer is often generic. Strengthen it by mentioning where you're going, how active you'll be, and any dress code you follow. A 9-to-5 office day calls for different clothing than a park walk with the kids, and the assistant uses these details to narrow the suggestion. Be specific but casual; you don't need a formal prompt, just real-life details. If Alexa+ doesn't pick up on something you said, restate it more directly ("I mean I sit at a desk most of the day"). Sometimes the assistant will ignore a detail — that's a known limitation, not a mistake on your part.
💬 Example: "I have meetings until 3 p.m., then I'm picking up the kids. I'm usually in business casual."
You'll know it worked when the next suggestion clearly reflects your situation — something like "wear layers, keep a blazer handy" — instead of a generic coat-and-boots answer.

## Step 3 — Ask for a backup plan for weather changes
Weather rarely stays put. Ask Alexa+ to plan for the worst case so you're not caught out by an unexpected cold snap, a sudden shower, or a temperature drop after sunset. Contingency questions like "what if it gets colder" are a useful test of how well the assistant handles multi-part requests. If your device doesn't seem to handle the contingency well, try breaking it into two shorter asks — first the morning outfit, then the evening backup. That usually works as a fallback.
💬 Example: "What if it gets colder in the evening, or if it rains on my way home?"
You'll know it worked when you get a **layered or contingency** suggestion — a cardigan to pack, a foldable umbrella, waterproof shoes — instead of just one fixed outfit.

## Step 4 — Tell Alexa+ to remember your preferences for next time
This is where the workflow gets genuinely useful. Ask Alexa+ to remember the preferences you just described — fit, colors you avoid, what counts as "too cold" for you — so future mornings don't require you to repeat them. Whether Alexa+ can save in-conversation preferences reliably may depend on your device, app version, and plan; if the in-conversation "remember" doesn't seem to stick, the same preferences can usually be set somewhere in the Alexa app's settings area (the exact label and location vary by app version and device — look for a section that mentions preferences, profile, or voice responses). The in-conversation route is faster when it works.
💬 Example: "Remember that I prefer layers, avoid bright colors, and run cold at anything under 60°F."
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ **confirms out loud** that it has saved your preferences, or when your next outfit question already reflects them without you repeating them.

## Step 5 — Make it part of your morning with a Routine
The biggest time-saver: turn this into an automatic briefing so you never have to ask. In the Alexa app, look for a section called **Routines** (it may be labeled "Your Routines" or appear under a "More" or menu area depending on your app version). Create a new Routine and set a time trigger for when you usually get ready — pick a time you'll reliably be near the device, not an optimistic "should be awake" time you never hit. Add a custom action that runs your outfit-and-weather request, with the preferences from Step 4 baked in. If a Routine step won't go through, the feature may be limited by your current plan or app version — check Amazon's official Alexa+ page for what's included.
💬 Example: Time trigger 7:15 a.m. → Custom action: "Give me today's forecast, my saved outfit preferences, and what I should wear today."
You'll know it worked when, at the chosen time, your Echo lights up **on its own** and delivers a weather-plus-outfit briefing without you saying a word.

## Common mistakes
- **Asking only one half of the question.** "What's the weather?" gets a forecast, not clothing ideas. Combine both in one sentence so Alexa+ treats it as a single task with two parts.
- **Skipping the "remember this" step.** Without saved preferences, you'll repeat yourself every morning — fine once, tiring by Wednesday. Save them once and reuse them all week.
- **Setting the Routine trigger too early.** If Alexa+ starts briefing you before you're actually awake, you'll mute or skip the Routine within a week. Pick a realistic time you reliably have the device nearby.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** A small morning ritual that gives you one less decision before coffee, and one less app to open before the door.
- **For your work or business:** If your work involves showing up somewhere — clients, school, events — a weather-aware suggestion cuts down on those days you walk out underdressed or overdressed.
- **If you're just getting started:** The easiest first move is just to ask once, today, and see what the assistant suggests. Refine from there based on what it gets right and what it misses.

## Try it now
Say it once, right now, while you're thinking about it: **"Alexa, what's the forecast for today, and what should I wear?"** Then refine the answer with one real detail from your day tomorrow. Two minutes today, and Wednesday morning is already half-handled.
